specification.problem: Success probability and optimal iteration count of a Grover-like two-reflection search (stand-in for the optimized quantum random-walk search) when the oracle and diffusion inversion phases carry systematic offsets: a = pi + d1, b = pi + d2, for one marked item among N = 2^n.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Single marked item, small n (<= 6, so n+1 <= 7 qubits). Build the generalized Grover iteration with phase-error offsets, one oracle query per iteration. Compute P_k from the exact 2x2 reduced matrix and compare it with the simulated marked-state frequency. Sweep k to find the maximizing k. The paper's specific optimized random-walk operator and tuned phase values are NOT recovered. Comparison with the Grover baseline uses the ideal Grover phases plus the same errors.

symbols.meaning: uniform superposition over all N items
overlap sin of the initial angle, \langle w|s\rangle=1/\sqrt{N}
number of iterations (equals number of oracle queries)

equations.label: Phase-inversion oracle and diffusion
equations.latex: O=I-(1-e^{ia})|w\rangle\langle w|,\quad D=I-(1-e^{ib})|s\rangle\langle s|=H^{\otimes n}\big(I-(1-e^{ib})|0\rangle\langle 0|\big)H^{\otimes n}
equations.description: Generalized phase-inversion oracle and diffusion. Ideal Grover uses a=b=pi, with a global sign on D.
equations.justification: Standard generalized amplitude-amplification operators. The abstract names phase inversions with errors but gives no formulas.
assumptions: Diffusion phase b is the same on every iteration

equations.label: Iteration operator and state
equations.description: Success probability after k iterations, with a=pi+delta_1 and b=pi+delta_2.
equations.abstract_quote: the relationship between the success rate of the algorithm, the database size, the number of iterations and the phase error is depicted
equations.justification: This relationship implies that P_k is a function of N, k and the errors. The explicit form here is my own construction.
assumptions: Optimized random-walk search is modeled as this two-reflection iteration

equations.label: Reduced 2x2 matrix in basis {|w>,|w_perp>}
equations.description: Q restricted to the invariant 2D plane, where |s> has real components (lambda, sqrt(1-lambda^2)).
equations.justification: The geometric picture in the abstract is the 2D invariant subspace. The matrix follows from eq_1.

equations.label: Eigen-decomposition form of P_k
equations.latex: Q\sim e^{i\gamma}\exp\!\big(-i\,\theta_{\rm eff}\,\hat n\cdot\vec\sigma\big),\quad P_k=\Big|\sum_{j=\pm}c_j e^{-ik\theta_j}\Big|^2=A\sin^2(k\theta_{\rm eff}+\phi)+\text{offset}
equations.description: Q is an SU(2) rotation times a phase, with eigenphases e^{-i theta_j}. P_k oscillates at theta_eff. A, phi and offset are computed numerically from the eigenvectors of eq_3, with cos(theta_eff)=Re tr(Q)/2 up to the phase.
equations.justification: The sketch proposes this form via Chebyshev/Bloch analysis. The abstract does not give it.
assumptions: Exact closed forms for A, phi, offset are not supplied; use numerical diagonalization

equations.label: Maximum success and optimal iteration count
equations.description: Maximum success rate and the iteration count that achieves it, found by a sweep over k.
equations.abstract_quote: we give both the maximum success rate of the algorithm and the required number of iterations when the algorithm is in the presence of phase errors
equations.justification: The abstract claims both quantities are given. The formula is inferred from the sin^2 form, and the rounding is an approximation.
assumptions: k_opt from the formula is approximate; verify with the sweep

registers.name: data
registers.role: indexes N=2^n items, little-endian integer encoding, marked item w as bitstring

registers.name: anc
registers.role: oracle ancilla in |-> for phase kickback; optional. Total qubits n+1 <= 7

specification.initial_state: All qubits |0>, then H on each data qubit gives |s>. The ancilla is prepared in |-> by X then H if used.

steps.description: Prepare |s> with H on the data qubits. Prepare the ancilla in |-> if the oracle is a kickback black box.
Repeat k times: apply the oracle with phase a=pi+delta_1 (one black-box query per iteration, or a controlled-phase with an adjustable angle).
Apply the diffusion: H^n, X^n, multi-controlled phase mcp(b) with b=pi+delta_2, X^n, H^n.
Classical sweep over k=0..K and over d. Compute the analytic P_k from the 2x2 matrix, find P_max and k_opt, and compare with the Grover baseline (ideal phases plus the same errors).

specification.measurement: Measure the n data qubits (not the ancilla) after k iterations. The frequency of the marked bitstring estimates P_k. Respect Qiskit little-endian bit order in the counts keys.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Sweep k, compare the simulated marked-state frequency or exact probability with the eq_2/eq_3 prediction, and select k maximizing P_k. Compare P_max(optimized) with P_max(Grover) for each error value.
assumptions: Phase errors are systematic and fixed on every application, with no random noise
Optimized random-walk search is modeled as a two-reflection iteration with a tunable diffusion phase, possibly plus a coin qubit
Oracle is queryable as a phase oracle or controlled phase with an adjustable angle
The tuned optimized phases are not known from the abstract and must be chosen by the implementer, e.g. by numerically maximizing the ideal P at about (pi/4)sqrt(N) iterations
